assessment.nobel_worthiness: A highly consequential body of work that transformed understanding of how technology and trade shocks reshape local labour demand and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson provide a coherent and identifiable core for the linked task, technology and China-shock evidence.
assessment.maturity: The empirical findings, mechanisms and wider influence have been extensively developed over many years.
uncertainties: The appropriate balance between the technology and trade components, and credit beyond this core, remains contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data have yielded a major new empirical account of intergenerational mobility and its geographic and institutional correlates.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren and Friedman are central to the research programme and its measurement infrastructure.
assessment.maturity: The research agenda is influential, replicated in extensions and directly important for public policy, though still developing.
uncertainties: The extent to which descriptive mobility measurement establishes causal policy mechanisms remains uneven.
Attribution across a broad collaborative programme is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The modern analysis of monopsony has substantially changed how economists interpret wage setting, labour-market concentration and labour policy.
assessment.attribution: Manning is the clearest single intellectual anchor for the modern monopsony framework.
assessment.maturity: A mature theoretical contribution with a large subsequent empirical literature and policy relevance.
uncertainties: The proposed grouping combines foundational theory with later empirical work whose credit assignment is less settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on fetal and early-life conditions has established that human-capital formation and later outcomes depend critically on early environments.
assessment.attribution: Currie, Almond and Cunha represent complementary empirical and dynamic-human-capital contributions.
assessment.maturity: The field has accumulated extensive evidence across settings and has enduring implications for education and health policy.
uncertainties: The candidate description covers heterogeneous mechanisms and methods, making a three-person attribution necessarily selective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic panel GMM methods became foundational tools for empirical economics when persistence and unobserved heterogeneity complicate causal analysis.
assessment.attribution: Arellano, Blundell and Bond have direct and closely connected claims to the core methods.
assessment.maturity: The methods are long established, broadly taught and continuously assessed in applied and methodological research.
uncertainties: Widespread application has also revealed sensitivity to instrument choice and specification.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification shifted attention from unjustified point identification to conclusions warranted under transparent, weaker assumptions.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the indispensable foundational contributor; the wider programme involves substantial additional credit.
assessment.maturity: The conceptual framework is mature and has diffuse influence across econometrics and empirical policy analysis.
uncertainties: Its impact is often methodological and indirect rather than concentrated in a single empirical discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The programme made taxable-income responses and modern administrative-data evidence central to the empirical study of optimal taxation.
assessment.attribution: Saez and Chetty are major contributors to the empirical and conceptual development, though the area has many essential contributors.
assessment.maturity: The work is established, consequential for tax design and supported by a substantial subsequent literature.
uncertainties: A unified attribution spanning elasticity measurement, optimal-tax theory and later administrative-data work is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Audit and correspondence designs made discrimination empirically visible and disciplined a large literature on unequal labour-market treatment.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan made a landmark contribution, while the method and evidence rest on a broad set of researchers including Charles.
assessment.maturity: The approach is longstanding, widely used and influential in both research and public debate.
uncertainties: Correspondence-study estimates identify treatment at particular stages of hiring rather than the full structure of labour-market inequality.
